Drug discovery is a hierarchical reinforcement-learning problem with a vast action space and years-long horizon. Scientists design and synthesize molecules that they predict will be potent, safe, and readily absorbed into the body, but this typically requires years of iteration in the lab and millions of dollars to develop a molecule that is ready for testing in human.

At Inductive, we're building the AI and machine learning tools to radically accelerate this process. Our state-of-the-art predictive models and medicinal chemistry agents identify the right compounds to make at the right time, while our AI-integrated lab shortens the time to synthesize and test them. Our ADMET/PK models have placed first in the world’s largest AI drug discovery competition for ADMET benchmarks three consecutive times, and our technology is already being applied across dozens of biopharma partnerships.

Introducing Kepler

The Problem

High-stakes industries are falling behind on AI adoption. Their workflows can’t afford wrong answers. And AI can’t be trusted to give right ones because of hallucinations. The barrier isn’t that the models aren’t smart enough. It’s that no one can verify what they produce. The fix isn’t a better model, it’s a trust layer: every output traceable, every calculation auditable, every answer reproducible.

What Kepler Is

Kepler is the agent harness - the infrastructure layer that wraps around AI models to make their outputs reliable, traceable, and verifiable. The model is a replaceable component. The harness is the product.

In Kepler's architecture, the LLM orchestrates - it decides what data to gather, what to compute, how to structure the output. But every actual data point, every extracted value, every calculation flows through deterministic code pipelines. The LLM never touches the data
